description: Business-day deadline (clear days, cutoffs, DST) on a named or caller calendar — Computes the date (and optionally the instant) a business-day deadline falls on, for an agent drafting or checking a contract, notice, SLA or partner response window: '10 clear business days' (both endpoints excluded) or 'within 10 business days' (end day counted), forward or backward, with an after-cutoff roll, caller or named holiday calendar and a DST-aware deadline time. Named calendars (US fe

calendar.description: Named holiday calendar with a source and supported date range (outside it the answer is unsupported), weekends-only (Saturday/Sunday only), or caller (only the holidays you list).

claimedDeadline.description: A deadline date someone asserted; the check fails with the computed date if it differs.

counting.description: clear: days strictly between start and deadline, so the deadline is business day N+1. elapsed: the deadline is business day N after start (the end day is counted).

cutoff.description: Local HH:MM. With a date-time start (direction after), a start strictly later than the cutoff, or on a non-business day, is deemed received on the next business day. 17:00 exactly is on time. Without cutoff there is no roll.

deadlineTime.description: Local HH:MM at which the deadline expires on the deadline date; needs timeZone to produce an instant.

direction.description: Default after. before counts backward from start (for 'at least N days before the hearing').

disambiguation.description: How to read a deadline time that falls in a DST gap (earlier: before-gap offset reading backward; later: shifted forward) or overlap (earlier/later occurrence). Without it, a gap or overlap returns unknown with both candidates.

holidays.description: Extra non-business dates YYYY-MM-DD (company closures, a calendar we do not carry).

start.description: Local date YYYY-MM-DD, or local date-time YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM[:SS] (the notice/receipt moment). Never read from the clock.

weekend.description: Non-business weekdays, 0=Sunday..6=Saturday. Default [0, 6]; use [5, 6] for a Friday/Saturday weekend.

name: business-deadline
